summary: Summit cabin built 1931, then a wooden tower replaced in 1934 by a 45 ft 9 in steel tower, per state reports; no source on today's site.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Cabin being erected on the summit; the 1930-32 report describes a 10 x 12 cabin
Wooden tower replaced with a 45-foot 9-inch steel tower, using ECW funds, per the 1932-34 state report

evidence.supports: November 1931: cabin being erected on top of the mountain near the McDowell-Rutherford line
evidence.quote: A cabin is being erected on top of Pinnacle Mountain near the McDowell-Rutherford line, which will be of aid in locating forest fires. The state department of conservation and development is co-operating in erecting the cabin

evidence.supports: 1930-32 report: 10 x 12 cabin, occupied by the lookout man on duty during fire season
evidence.quote: A 10 x 12 cabin was erected, the cabin is occupied by the lookout man on duty during fire season.

evidence.supports: May 1932: steel tower planned to replace the wood structure, $700 to $900
evidence.quote: A steel tower to replace the present wood structure on Pinnacle mountain, Rutherford county, is being planned. This tower will cost between $700 and $900.

evidence.supports: November 1932: 47-foot steel tower costing $850 to be erected soon
evidence.quote: A steel fire lookout tower, 47 feet high and costing $850, will be erected soon on Pinnacle Mountain in Rutherford county.

evidence.supports: Cost split between the state and Rutherford County with a lumber company
evidence.quote: One half the expense will be paid by the state forest service and one half by Rutherford county and the Hutton-Bourbonnais Lumber company.

evidence.supports: Part of the state's fire protection program in the South Mountain area
evidence.quote: The tower is to be a unit in the department's fire protection program in the South Mountain area of Burke and Rutherford counties.

evidence.supports: 1934: wooden tower replaced by a 45-foot 9-inch steel tower using ECW funds (design, height, event)
evidence.quote: The wooden tower was replaced with a 45-foot 9-inch steel tower using ECW funds.

evidence.supports: Agency listed for the North Carolina section of the page
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A November 1932 newspaper planned a 47-foot tower; the 1934 state report gives 45 feet 9 inches for the tower that replaced the wooden one, so the report's figure is used.

notes_for_editor: One compiled page quoting 1931-34 newspapers and state reports; not checked against the originals. The height on record, 13.9 m, is the 1934 state-report figure of 45 ft 9 in. The 47 ft figure from the November 1932 newspaper was the planned height, not the built one. Status, access and today's site are not in any source read. Search surfaced a 1931 Rutherford County lookout named for fire warden C.E. Biggerstaff near the 1924 burn zone, and a 'Biggerstaff Mountain' entry in a compilation; neither was read, so they may be a different tower and should be checked before any merge. The Tennessee Pinnacle Mountain tower on Buffalo Mountain is a different structure. Search used 2 WebSearch calls.
